source_text: Hi, I was going to go listen to some of my Anders EP recordings but I forgot how that works
reply_text:
㊥ (how it works) The EPs play on phone2. In Termux there, run `sh a.sh`. It starts the little web server on port 8000 if it isn't already up, then opens `http://127.0.0.1:8000/index.html` in the phone's browser, where you pick an EP and play it in `player.html`. To take notes from Emacs, turn on `M-x anders-np-mode`.

🈖 (the pieces) Everything is in `~/notes/anders-eps/`:
- `a.sh` (the copy on the phone) needs `~/anders-eps` on phone2 to exist, and runs `~/anders/serve.py 8000`. Its log goes to `~/anders/http.log`.
- Each time you play, pause or change track, `player.html` sends that to the server, and the server streams it on `/nowplaying/stream`.
- `anders-np.el` follows that stream over the reverse tunnel (`ssh -p 2223 u0_a318@localhost`). Your mode line then shows something like `♪07 3/14 Isaiah 28, rough`, with ‖ when paused.
- With the mode on, `<next>` (PgDn) during playback asks for a note and adds it, timestamped, under that track in `listening-notes.org`. You last added notes there on Nov 9 and 10, for EP03.

㊩ (tunnel) Just now, ssh to port 2223 got "Connection refused", so phone2's reverse tunnel isn't up. The mode line will stay blank until it is. Playback itself only needs the phone. If the tunnel didn't come up when Termux started, run `phone-tunnel.sh` on phone2 to bring it back.
